speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me if you've had any recent headaches, neck stiffness, or sensitivity to light along with your fever and confusion? Also, have you experienced any seizures or recent travel?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of tics and current use of haloperidol, I need to ask if you've noticed any muscle stiffness, high fever spikes, or tremors recently that might suggest a reaction to the medication. Also, have you experienced any changes in your bowel movements, such as constipation, or difficulty swallowing?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text: Your symptoms of high fever, generalized rigidity, and altered mentation while taking haloperidol are highly concerning for Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. To confirm this diagnosis and rule out other causes, I need to check your muscle enzyme levels and blood counts immediately. REQUEST TEST: CK_LEVEL, CBC, BMP.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: White Blood Cell Count: 14,700/mm3 (elevated); Creatine Kinase: 5600 U/L (elevated); Urine Toxicology: Negative; Brain MRI: Unremarkable; CSF Opening Pressure: 22 cm H2O; CSF White Blood Cells: 4 cells/mm3; CSF Red Blood Cells: 0 cells/mm3; CSF Glucose: 64 mg/dL; CSF Protein: 48 mg/dL; Serum Glucose: 96 mg/dL.

speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated Creatine Kinase of 5600 U/L, combined with your fever, rigidity, and altered mentation while on haloperidol, strongly confirms Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome
